source.title: Bypassing Safety Alignment via API Design: A Systematic Risk Analysis of Response Prefill in LLM Systems
source.authors: Ya-Kai Li; Jie-Kang Hu; Wei-Duan Sang; Lu-Ping Ma; Dong-Sheng Nie; Wei-Juan Zhang; Ai-Min Yu; Yi Su; Qing-Jia Huang; Qi-Hang Zhou

record.file_problem: The text appears to be a complete paper. Its title, “Prefill-level Jailbreak: A Black-Box Risk Analysis of Large Language Models,” differs from the supplied title; the text identifies itself as arXiv:2504.21038v2.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether assistant-response prefilling can increase harmful compliance, using API attack-success rates rather than the original studies’ fine-tuning or KL-divergence methods.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates response-prefill attacks and a prompt-suffix control. It does not evaluate harmful or benign fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base per-position KL, weight localization, or safety-deepening training. The first-token probability analysis compares prefill with no prefill, not aligned and base models across response positions.
record.test_reason: It measures harmful-compliance rates when the assistant response is prefilled with a compliant or refusal-then-pivot opening. It covers 14 safety-aligned API models on AdvBench, with irrelevant-prefill and prompt-instruction controls. This directly tests V4's prefilling part, using a different model set and a model judge rather than the original's HEx-PHI setup. It does not test fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base KL, localization, causes or deepening.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that response prefilling is a widespread jailbreak surface across all 14 models, with adaptive prefills exceeding 99% ASR on several. They say it works by shifting first-token probability from refusal to compliance, and that it adds 10–15 points to PAIR/ReNeLLM. They also conclude that generic content filters and system prompts give limited protection, while a detector of the prompt–prefill manipulative relationship works better.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses black-box API response prefilling and jailbreak-success measurements, not harmful/benign fine-tuning or aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by victim model, attack category, static versus adaptive optimization, evaluation metric, and defense. The study reports that adaptive attacks generally outperform static templates; prompt suffixes perform poorly in the ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Prefill shifts first-token probability mass from refusal tokens (about 0.86–0.91 baseline, minus about 0.49) toward compliance tokens (about 0.01 baseline, plus about 0.25) in GPT-3.5-turbo and DeepSeek-V3. Method-level shifts correlate with ASR (R²=0.854).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefilling bypasses refusal by flipping the first-token refusal-versus-compliance distribution. This is a mechanism for V4, not evidence on aligned-versus-base KL concentration (V3).

record.peer_reviewed: Dependable Systems and Networks (as stated in supplied metadata)
record.problems: The mechanism analysis is black-box and limited to two representative models; the paper notes it lacks white-box validation. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the supplied text. The attack-success results depend in part on a Gemini-2.5-Pro model judge.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row cap is reached. Omitted results include Table III string-match values and categories other than Refusal Bypass; most of the per-model PAIR+Prefill and ReNeLLM+Prefill results in Table IV; and defense results in Tables VII–IX. The selected Table IV rows retain the explicitly discussed Gemini-2.5-Flash PAIR example, a range of PAIR comparisons, and several ReNeLLM comparisons. R37 duplicates the same explicitly stated Gemini-2.5-Flash comparison recorded from Table IV; it is retained as the text-stated example, while R38 records the table value and should be treated as duplicate evidence, not an independent condition.

untested.parts: No aligned-versus-base per-token KL. First-token probability is compared only with versus without prefill.

Adversarial (optimized) suffixes and decoding changes are not tested. Prefill length or depth is not varied. Table III has no no-prefill ASR baseline per model; a control exists only for DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-3.5-turbo.
No analysis of the data or objective causing shallowness.
No deepening training; it is only proposed as future work.

missing.what: Per-model MJ ASR for the six non-refusal-bypass prefill categories. Several are low on stronger models, e.g. Gemini-2.5-Pro persona 11.32/15.81, Claude-Sonnet-4 persona 15.38/20.15, GPT-4 commitment 14.22/21.56. These bear on how much prefill content matters for V4.
Post-defense ASR under Llama-Guard, System-Prompt-Guard and Prompt-Detection. These show prefill attacks still succeed at roughly 20–90% after defenses on DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-3.5.

record.verdict_notes: The text's title is 'Prefill-level Jailbreak: A Black-Box Risk Analysis of Large Language Models.' The prefill evidence partly overlaps V4's original source (2406.05946), but this is an independent study, so verdicts apply. The judge (Gemini-2.5-Pro) is also a victim model and the adaptive attacker, which may bias its own scores. Many PAIR+Prefill values in the record were taken from the ReNeLLM+Prefill column; corrected values remain far above PAIR alone, so states are unchanged. The 'challenges' label on the prompt-suffix control is removed because that control is an instruction, not an adversarial suffix. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and whether a few to a few hundred examples remove refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions, including whether it is concentrated in the first few positions.
Decoding changes were not tested. The study tests response prefills and a prompt-suffix instruction; it does not test every possible compliant opening or suffix.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or training objectives produce shallow safety behaviour.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether that training remains robust.

relationships.condition: Refusal-bypass prefill (static and adaptive) on Gemini-2.5-Flash, Qwen, Llama-4, GPT-3.5, DeepSeek, Mistral and Kimi; static/adaptive aggregates on GPT-3.5 and DeepSeek-V3 versus irrelevant-prefill controls; prefill added to PAIR/ReNeLLM on all listed models
relationships.reason: MJ ASR is 83–98.5% in R01–R02, R05–R14 and R17–R24. R34–R36 reach 91–99.6% against 4–8% controls. Adding prefill raises PAIR from 24–80% to 81–99% (R37, R39–R51) and ReNeLLM by 7–18 points (R52–R56).
relationships.display_finding: ASR was 83–98.5% for individual prefill settings and 91–99.6% in the aggregates against 4–8% for irrelevant prefills, and adding a prefill raised PAIR from 24–80% to 81–99% and ReNeLLM by 7–18 points.
